editorial.summary: Khalyla joins the recurring cast for a long first-person account of her background, a previous consensually non-monogamous household, meeting Bobby Lee on Tinder, their attraction and negotiated sexual role-play, his sobriety, and the possibility of a family. The hosts repeatedly turn her account into racial, sexual and relationship theories; the record preserves those ideas but distinguishes Khalyla's testimony, jokes, disputed claims, fantasy role-play, coercive advice and factual assertions. The closing third shifts to nursing, the historical paid-date bit, Bobby's career and a long improvised trivia game.
source_notes: The raw file contains 4,973 segments and approximately 27,505 words; the clean file contains 4,968 segments and the same approximate word count across 8,363.88 seconds.
All five cleaner removals are empty zero-duration artifacts. This is an unusually clean ASR pass structurally; its remaining problems are names, local phrase recovery and editorial interpretation.
The title and speech repeatedly render Khalyla phonetically as `Kalilah`; the canonical public spelling is Khalyla.

CDC describes 2009 H1N1 as a novel influenza A virus and notes that symptoms generally resemble seasonal influenza. The episode supplies only a self-diagnosis by web search, not a clinical result: https://archive.cdc.gov/www_cdc_gov/flu/pandemic-resources/2009-h1n1-pandemic.html

The dialogue itself is the primary source for Khalyla's account of her upbringing, relationships and work. External biographical aggregation is deliberately not used to expose private relatives or former partners.
Sony identifies the sequel as `22 Jump Street`; the cast also corrects the title in the next turn: https://www.sonypictures.com/movies/22jumpstreet
ABC identifies Eric Stonestreet as the actor who played Cameron on Modern Family: https://abc.com/shows/modern-family/about-the-show/1000

The episode's offensive, explicit, coercive, implausible, contradictory and wrong ideas remain represented. Public restrictions protect private people, minor sexual history and intimate details; they do not censor ideas.
editorial.speaker_policy: Recurring voices can often be inferred by a human and the episode names its guest, but the canonical artifact has no accepted identity windows or independently held-out multispeaker result. Named dialogue remains withheld.
